course_description:
This course provides an in-depth analysis of financial institution management. It covers the business activities of financial institutions and methods for measuring and managing their risk exposures.

Banks and other financial institutions, who support the flow of money through the economy, operate so fundamentally differently from any other type of company that require a course of study all of their own to understand their function. Financial Institutions and Markets" provides a comprehensive overview of the core functions, operations, and regulatory environments of modern financial entities. One particularly important consideration in the study of financial institutions is the range of unique risks facing these firms. A primary focus of the course, which is where the syllabus begins, is the identification, measurement, and strategic management of these unique risks. Students will explore operational frameworks for understanding and managing risks faced by financial institutions, such as liquidity risk management, credit risk analysis, asset-liability management, loan portfolio concentration. Following this, the course covers ideas related to the market operations performed by financial institutions, which includes securitisation and off-balance-sheet operations. The course finished with a look at certain regulations, known as capital adequacy requirements, that financial institutions have to abide by in an effort to protect the wider economy from systemic collapse.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with a deep understanding of the management of financial institutions. The skills and knowledge gained in this course will enable students to understand the roles of financial institutions in financial markets, analyse their business operations, including lending activities, and manage various types of risks they face, such as liquidity risk, interest rate risk, and credit risk.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and contrast different types of financial institutions and their functions within society, and distinguish the levels of regulation for these institutions.
Examine in detail the on and off balance sheet products of financial institutions.
Translate the balance sheet activities of financial institutions and select the appropriate risk mitigation techniques to preserve capital or profitability.
Demonstrate through application how liquidity, interest rate and credit risks can be mitigated for financial institutions.
Differentiate financial institution off-balance sheet activities, including securitisation and derivatives, and apply these activities to different scenario settings.
